title: The Workbench on a Real Repo
service: RealRepo: the lesson's before/after benchmark on its sample app. The five outcomes are measured from what each scripted run left behind (feedback records with per-test results, the diff, the handoff packet, the review), every repetition's outcomes are kept in SQLite, the two pipelines are compared run by run, a live timeline streams when each run reaches its milestones (time-to-first-meaningful-edit, first test run, acceptance) as CSV, and the repo's import graph decides which tests a change can affect
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no model and no network: both pipelines are scripted, and every run, event stream and repository snapshot is data the tests hand in

parts.lesson_anchor: The five outcomes measured (tests_actually_run: most 'tests passed' claims are unverifiable; acceptance_met: the test that proves the goal must be the test that ran; files_outside_scope; handoff_quality; reviewer_total) and the lesson's table for the two runs; code/main.py run_prompt_only and run_workbench, which hard-code the outcomes instead of measuring them; the artifacts they read: lesson 37's feedback record and its null exit (no exit, no progress), lesson 40's seven handoff fields and its next_action rule, lesson 39's five 0-2 scores out of 10
planted_bugs: load_feedback leaves results as None for a command that runs no tests (the init script, the verification gate), against FeedbackRecord's docstring; the AttributeError surfaces two calls later, in latest_results under measure -> tests_actually_run
tests_actually_run falls back to the agent's claim when a run has no feedback records, so the lesson's prompt-only run, which never runs a test but says tests_passed, counts as having run them
latest_results keeps 'skipped' results, against its docstring, so a pytest run that skipped the acceptance test (exit code 0, nothing ran) counts as tests_actually_run

handoff_quality grades a packet that has every field but next_action as partial; lesson 40 calls it a status report, not a handoff, so it is missing; a blank next_action is not filled in either, so a presence check is not enough
parts.timing_assert: 200 acceptance selectors (test functions) against a 2,000-result suite run (20 modules x 25 functions x 4 parametrized cases) under 0.15 s. acceptance_met checks every selector against every result through covers(), and covers() builds the node's ancestors with PurePosixPath(...).parents each time: 400,000 calls. Measured on this machine (Python 3.12.14, load average 4 to 9, other agents running): the starter with the other four bugs fixed 1.55-2.58 s over 12 runs in 6 processes and 1.60-2.52 s in three checker runs, at least 10x the limit; the reference, which indexes every result's ancestors once, median 8.3-10.4 ms and at most 17 ms over 300 runs, under 1/8 of the limit. Fixes that stay quadratic but drop the per-call cost pass clearly: lru_cache on ancestors 35-53 ms, a set of ancestors per result 14-29 ms, startswith with a boundary check 14-33 ms
parts.overfix_guard: a selector looked up as an exact node id (a test function must cover its parametrized cases, a module its tests); str.startswith without a boundary (test_signup would cover test_signup_happy_path); an index keyed by test module (a test selector would answer for its failing neighbours, and pytest -k happy would meet acceptance); an index that keeps each selector's last result only (sample_app holds a failing test); records with any non-zero exit skipped (a command that exits 1 still ran its tests); the shipped exit_code None check lost while rewriting latest_results (a pytest run the runner killed after it printed two passes, lesson 37: no exit, no progress); a selector that covers no test that ran counted as met (all() over nothing: the prompt-only row, a skipped acceptance test); an empty list counted as an unfilled handoff field (the workbench packet's failed_attempts: []); every unfilled field graded missing (a blank verdict_pointer is partial)

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It: comparison.json and before-after-report.md carry the outcomes per pipeline; Exercise 4 (with a real model the outcomes get noisier, so the same task is repeated and every repetition kept); the skill's CI job that fails when workbench outcomes regress on a fixed task suite
parts.storage: SQLite, one row per outcome: (run, pipeline, outcome, value) with an autoincrement seq for recording order; the value is JSON text, so bool, int, str and list come back as the same types
parts.exactness: outcomes read back equal type for type (exact() tells True from 1 and a list from a tuple), before and after a close and reopen: True and False flags, reviewer_total 10 and 0, an empty files_outside_scope, a file list in the order given (not sorted) with a comma and a semicolon inside paths ('docs/notes, v2.md', 'docs/a;b.md'), handoff_quality 'missing' as a value; two repetitions of the same pipeline (r2 and r10) keep their own outcomes
traps: flags stored as 0 and 1 (SQLite has no boolean, and 1 == True hides it from ==)
files stored one row per path, so an empty list leaves no row to rebuild the outcome from
files joined with ';' or ','
files sorted on the way in or out
runs ordered by run id ('r10' before 'r2') or left to an unordered SELECT DISTINCT
outcomes ordered by run and pipeline instead of recording order
an unknown pipeline, an impossible handoff level or a total of 11 accepted
clarifying_questions: the same run and pipeline twice

parts.lesson_anchor: The two pipelines (same task, same sample app, two runs); Read the before/after report and decide which surfaces gave the most leverage; the skill's hard rejects (a benchmark with only one pipeline; percentages without a denominator, always n / m; reports that hide false negatives); Exercise 3 (the false-negative pass)
parts.algorithm: pair runs by id and list the unpaired; per outcome count workbench better, prompt-only better and tie in the outcome's own units and direction (flags as 1 and 0, files by count with fewer better, handoff as an ordinal missing < partial < full packet, the reviewer total as it is); the median of the per-run differences; no_gain = the paired runs where the workbench did better on nothing
traps: runs paired by position, so one unpaired run shifts every pair after it
the paired runs zipped in the order each pipeline's records arrive (r4's workbench record comes last, r7's right after r4's prompt-only)
unpaired runs counted
handoff levels compared as text ('partial' > 'full packet' > 'missing')
file lists compared as lists (lexicographic) or more files counted as better
the difference of the two pipelines' medians, or the mean, instead of the median of per-run differences
no_gain taken as the runs where prompt-only won something (misses the all-tie run)
no paired run answered with an empty report instead of ValueError
parts.integration: the lesson's two scripted runs measured by Part 1, recorded three times in Part 2's store and compared from store.outcomes()
clarifying_questions: files by list or by count

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 1 (a sixth outcome, time-to-first-meaningful-edit, and how to measure it cleanly); the two pipelines' steps happen over time (init, scope, state, edit, acceptance through the feedback runner, gate); Part 1's rules for tests_actually_run and acceptance_met applied to the records so far
parts.wire_format: CSV, decided by the test's csv.reader over each yielded string and over their join: the header pipeline,milestone,t_ms, then one csv.writer record per milestone the moment a run reaches it (first_meaningful_edit, tests_run, acceptance_met), t_ms from the event, and an empty t_ms for each milestone a run never reached, written when that run's events end; every string ends with its line ending
traps: runs read one after another or in turns (the workbench stream waits on an event the test sets only after the prompt-only run's last record; the test's 2 s limit reports a stall)
unreached milestones held until every run has ended

edits compared as text (the spacing edit), as text without whitespace or with whole-line comments dropped (the comment edit, which also adds a trailing comment), with '#...' removed by a regex (which also eats README.md#signup inside a string literal), or with blank-line tokens or ast line numbers kept (the spacing edit adds a blank line)
edits outside the contract counted (a real code change to sample_app/settings.py)
the agent's claim counted as a test run
a killed record (exit_code None) meeting acceptance
two milestones reached by one event reported out of MILESTONES order (a one-run stream whose first pytest run already meets acceptance)
times from the clock instead of the event's t_ms
clarifying_questions: a file that does not parse

parts.lesson_anchor: The sample app (app.py and the test that imports it); acceptance_met: the test that proves the goal must be the test that ran, which here also means it must reach the code the change touched; the skill's rule that a project without an acceptance command gets no benchmark
traps: from a.b import c read as an attribute only (from sample_app import validators, from . import errors, from .. import app)
relative imports in an __init__.py resolved from the parent package (from .routes import router)
only top-level statements read (errors.py imports validators inside a function to avoid the cycle)
import lib.util without lib/__init__.py, which imports config
direct importers only
the validators <-> errors cycle
a changed test file left out, or a README change affecting tests
a module named testing.py counted as a test (test files start with test_; the helper is reached from validators)
proves_change comparing the whole selector with the test file
a directory selector matched without a path boundary (not in the test data; the interviewer asks)

deviations: Part 1 keeps the suggested acceptance-by-node-id idea, and plants the measurement's own defects as four stacked bugs: a None results field from load_feedback that surfaces two calls later, the fallback to the agent's claim, skipped results counted as tests that ran, and lesson 40's next_action rule. Records with exit_code None stay correct in the starter and are an overfix guard: lesson 40's exam already plants a None exit code in its Part 1. The suggested allowed/forbidden/soft split is dropped: the lesson calls README.md forbidden-zone bait, not a soft doc file, and lesson 36's exam already grades forbidden, off-scope and soft-off-scope files. files_outside_scope stays the lesson's single list of paths the contract does not allow.

The Part 1 timing defect moved. Re-running both pipelines and re-parsing the records for each of the report's five rows costs a constant 5x, which cannot be 8 times over a limit and 8 times under it. The slow path is now acceptance_met checking every selector against every result; the module-level and parametrized selectors from the suggested guard are the overfix checks.

Part 2 follows the suggestion (SQLite, one row per outcome, every repetition kept, types unchanged), but the pairing moved to Part 3, which pairs (run, pipeline, outcome) records itself; the store hands them back in recording order. Two traps are left out on purpose: a rejected outcome leaving some of its rows behind, and a second record for the same run and pipeline replacing the first. This chapter's exams already use both trap classes more than twice; the docstring still says a rejected outcome stores nothing, and the interviewer answers the duplicate question.

Part 4 is not the suggested concurrent run in isolated copies of the sample app: lesson 20's exam already streams isolated parallel episodes as CSV, with the same gate probe and cleanup traps. Part 4 is the lesson's Exercise 1 instead: time-to-first-meaningful-edit, measured live from both runs' event streams read at the same time, next to the first test run and acceptance. The output stays CSV.

Paths are written from the repo root that holds sample_app/; code/main.py mixes README.md and sample_app/... in the prompt-only run's touched list. Its unused FORBIDDEN set becomes the contract's forbidden list, and forbidden files count as outside scope, as in the lesson's table.
Part 5 follows the suggestion (import graph, relative imports, package __init__.py, a changed test file, a docs-only change) and adds proves_change, which reuses Part 1's selector rules.
